changelog: [When to Segment]: Added three concrete permissive rules to increase splitting frequency: (1) internal sentence-final punctuation ('.', '?') anywhere mid-utterance is always a mandatory split candidate, not only at the very end; (2) causal/additive connectives (그래서/그러니까/그런데/근데) mark a valid split point as soon as the preceding clause has a complete predicate, even if what follows is short or trails off — a short/incomplete remainder is never a reason to withhold the split; (3) coordinate -고/-며 clauses with independently resolved subjects/objects on each side are a valid split point without waiting for later material.

[Never Segment]: Narrowed the causal/result connective prohibition so it only blocks a split when clause B has NOT YET reached any predicate at all (a bare fragment) — removed the broader 'shares implicit subject' clause that was causing over-cautious under-segmentation; once B reaches its own complete predicate, splitting is allowed even with a shared subject. Also added a clarifying sentence restricting the conditional-chain prohibition strictly to the '…하고 … -면/-거든' pattern so it no longer discourages ordinary -고 coordination between two already-complete predicates, which is now explicitly permitted under [When to Segment].
